intro.text: Three assessment grading screens, three directions each. Every board is live: score items, clear a result, acknowledge a shortfall, switch judgement stage, stage a cohort decision. Each has a Light/Dark toggle in its top bar — dark is layered charcoal per FDR-012, not an inversion. Colour, type and spacing come from the app's own theme.css tokens. Nothing here invents a backend field that does not exist.

n1a.text:
1A · SINGLE COLUMN RUN — No category rail. One scroll in syllabus order, sticky category headers carrying their own progress. Two verdicts only; Clear appears after a result and warns that it erases the assessor and time (the DB constraint really does). Four chrome bands collapse to one line plus a live mat bar.
Spends: item_counts, per-item assessor attribution on every row, display_range.
Costs: long syllabi mean a long scroll; no peripheral view of far categories.

n1b.text:
1B · FOCUS RUNNER — One requirement, full bleed, readable at arm's length. Oversized targets, advance on mark, category strip above, a Jump to sheet and a list escape hatch. Built for a tablet held one-handed on the mat.
Spends: requirement_notes as real coaching text, display_range, per-category counts.
Costs: no overview while working; wrong for a desk reviewer; ten taps to see ten items.

n1c.text:
1C · LEDGER SHEET — The WKSA paper chart, digitised. Rows are requirements, categories are row bands, P/F are cells, notes are inline fields, and a rollup rail sits alongside. Keyboard legend in the header (↑↓ P F N).
Spends: item_counts and the category breakdown from the server, display_range, assessor + time on every row.
Costs: densest of the three; smallest touch targets; least suited to a phone.

n2a.text:
2A · EXCEPTION REPORT — Inverts the emphasis. What passed is one line and a disclosure; the screen is the shortfalls, each with its note and assessor, each needing confirmation before the seal unlocks. No percentages anywhere — results are three-valued, so a percentage was always a fiction.
Spends: the outcomes summary endpoint, per-item attribution, item provenance (link back to syllabus).
Costs: a clean assessment has almost nothing to look at.

n2b.text:
2B · CERTIFICATE PROOF — Renders the record as the document it becomes, so you proofread rather than fill in a form. Core areas, Techniques and Forms ledgers, the notes, and a seal line that is blank until sealed. Provenance and counts sit alongside.
Spends: generated_by, generated_at, started_at/completed_at, source_age_band, display_range — all currently unrendered.
Costs: longest to read; the proof is only as good as the reader.

n2c.text:
2C · INLINE SEAL STRIP — No route change and no mode swap. Completion is an in-page banner on the scoring screen that expands into a review strip, reusing the FDR-040 session-transition pattern already accepted rather than inventing a second one. The list dims behind it and scroll position survives.
Spends: the category breakdown from the server, item_counts.
Costs: least ceremony for the most permanent action in the app.

n3a.text:
3A · ONE DRAWER, TWO STAGES — One component replaces both drawers. The same sealed evidence sits at the top in both stages; below it swaps between Propose and Ratify, and at Ratify the instructor's proposal appears as a sealed quote above the Master's own controls. Click the stage tabs to compare.
Spends: gives the proposing instructor the evidence ledger only the Master sees today.
Costs: still a drawer — capped height, roster context is dimmed not usable.

n3b.text:
3B · DECISION LEDGER PAGE — Judgement leaves the drawer for a route: one vertical record of four dated entries — assessment sealed, proposal, decision, promotion. Sealed entries are muted and locked; the live one is gold. The promotion entry states its preconditions instead of hiding.
Spends: decided_at/proposed_at, the override flag, the promotion eligibility rules as visible copy.
Costs: loses the roster entirely; a route and a navigation model to build.

n3c.text:
3C · COHORT ADJUDICATION BOARD — Built for the real shape of the job: a Master finalising fourteen candidates in one sitting, not opening fourteen drawers. Rows carry evidence, proposal and an inline decision; the right pane holds the one in focus. Decisions stage, then write one row at a time with per-row failures, per FDR-028.
Spends: outcome filters, proposal attribution, per-row error handling.
Costs: invites speed over care; the proposal flow still needs its own surface.
